title: Best Blog and Article Writers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a blog or article writer: what the order should include, how to write the brief, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: A good article answers a reader's question better than the pages already ranking for it, in your brand's voice. Most disappointing orders come from a one-line brief, unclear rules on AI use, or text copied from other sites. This guide shows you how to order posts you can publish with confidence.

faq.q: Can the writer use AI tools?
faq.a: Some writers use AI for research or drafts, others do not use it at all. Decide what you accept, say so in the brief, and ask the writer to confirm before ordering. Whatever the process, the facts must be checked and the text must be original.

faq.q: Will the articles be optimized for search?
faq.a: Only if you ask. Give the writer the main search phrase and the question the reader has. Many writers also add headings, a meta description and internal link suggestions.
Normally the buyer receives the rights once the order is complete, but confirm it. Also ask whether the writer wants to show the piece in their portfolio, and whether you mind.

faq.q: How do I check the article is original?
faq.a: Run it through a plagiarism checker before publishing, and search a few exact sentences in a search engine. Also check every fact, number and quote against a reliable source.

faq.q: Should I order one article or a package?
faq.a: Start with one article to test the writer's research, style and speed. If it works, a package of several posts on a plan is usually easier to manage.
